formula: If / when / as soon as / until + present simple, ... will + verb
formula_visual: [If it rains], [we'll stay home] // [I'll call you] [when I arrive]
when_to_use: For real, likely future situations: the condition/time clause uses the PRESENT simple, and the result uses WILL. Same rule after time words: when, as soon as, before, after, until.
when_to_use_ar: لمواقف مستقبلية واقعية محتملة: جملة الشرط/الزمن بالمضارع البسيط، والنتيجة بـ will. نفس القاعدة بعد كلمات الزمن: when, as soon as, until.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Learners put 'will' in BOTH halves ('If it will rain, we will stay') because Arabic uses a future marker in the condition too. English keeps the if/when clause in the present simple.

examples.en: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
I'll call you when I arrive.
As soon as she finishes, we'll leave.
We won't start until everyone is here.
If you study hard, you'll pass.

common_errors.wrong: If it will rain, we will stay home.
common_errors.correct: If it rains, we'll stay home.
common_errors.explanation: The if-clause uses the present simple, not will.

common_errors.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
common_errors.correct: I'll call you when I arrive.
common_errors.explanation: After 'when' for the future, use the present simple.

common_errors.wrong: We will start until everyone comes.
common_errors.correct: We won't start until everyone comes.
common_errors.explanation: 'until' needs the negative result here + present simple.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: I'll text you as soon as I ___ (get) home.
If it ___ (be) sunny tomorrow, we'll go to the beach.
We won't leave until the rain ___ (stop).

quick_rule: If/when + PRESENT simple, ... WILL + verb. Never 'will' in the if/when half.
quick_rule_ar: If/when + مضارع بسيط، ... WILL + فعل. لا تضع 'will' في نصف الشرط.
mnemonic: The 'if/when' half stays in the present; only the result gets 'will'.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 4 you practised weak 'if', 'll, and the comma pause. Say: 'If it rains, // we'll stay home' — weak 'if', clear pause at the comma, contracted 'we'll'.
